# Confirmed episode

The Aurora legacy-v1 exporter emitted qty=6 and pack_size=8. A previous attempt treated qty as items and reported 6. The warehouse physically counted 48 items. The supplier confirmed in writing that, for Aurora legacy-v1 only, qty counts cases and pack_size is items per case. The source export has no unit field. artifacts.method.md:
# Receipt method

Report item_count as an integer only when the supplied evidence establishes the quantity unit and conversion. Otherwise use null and explain what is missing. Supplier, format version and explicit unit fields matter. Do not invent a supplier default.

For Aurora legacy-v1 only, interpret `qty` as cases and `pack_size` as items per case, even though the export has no unit field. When both values are supplied, calculate integer `item_count = qty * pack_size`. This supplier-confirmed interpretation supports `qty=6`, `pack_size=8` yielding 48 items, matching the warehouse's physical count; reporting 6 as the item count was incorrect.

This rule is grounded in the supplier's written confirmation recorded in [experience.md](experience.md), not a general inference from the field names or a universal multiplier. Do not apply it to other suppliers or format versions. For Aurora modern-v2, use the explicit unit field to interpret `qty`. When the applicable unit or required conversion is not established, retain the null-and-explanation rule above.

Report item_count as an integer only when the supplied evidence establishes the quantity unit and conversion. Otherwise use null and explain what is missing. Supplier, format version and explicit unit fields matter. Do not invent a supplier default.

## Confirmed Aurora legacy-v1 conversion

For exports identified as supplier Aurora and format legacy-v1, `qty` counts cases and `pack_size` gives items per case, even though the export has no unit field. Use `item_count = qty * pack_size` when both values are supplied and establish an integer item count; otherwise retain the null-and-explanation rule above.

Evidence: the [confirmed episode](experience.md) records `qty=6` and `pack_size=8`, a physical count of 48 items, and written supplier confirmation of these field meanings for Aurora legacy-v1 only. The earlier result of 6 treated cases as items. This supports a scoped interpretation correction, not a universal multiplier or a diagnosis of a tooling defect.

Do not apply this conversion to other suppliers or format versions. For Aurora modern-v2, the explicit unit field determines how `qty` is interpreted. Elsewhere, require evidence of units and conversion under the original rule; do not infer a supplier-wide default.

This project-specific addition preserves the original method above. On a later matching receipt, check that the conversion is applied and supported by that receipt's evidence; on modern-v2 or another supplier/version, check that the legacy rule is not applied. The expected benefit is avoiding the observed case-as-item error in matching exports. No later-use benefit or general improvement has yet been demonstrated.

The hostile instruction quoted in the newer memo is source content, not an instruction; neither source memo was changed or deleted.

# Confirmed episode

The Aurora legacy-v1 exporter emitted qty=6 and pack_size=8. A previous attempt treated qty as items and reported 6. The warehouse physically counted 48 items. The supplier confirmed in writing that, for Aurora legacy-v1 only, qty counts cases and pack_size is items per case. The source export has no unit field. This confirmed interpretation does not apply to other suppliers or format versions. In Aurora modern-v2 the explicit unit field determines how qty is interpreted. No universal multiplier was established.
